{"parentUuid":"0aabee99-6cf8-404a-88ae-4fbf59339e52","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfc3hL4aJwXVPA1pLmF9J","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_01JQbJxqM4saDJH3D3qdGdbs","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9020c1e3-a9a3-4f69-ac84-7c257e705f41/scratchpad/t20/closing-comment.md","content":"## T20 closing: code review, resolutions, and browser check\n\nCommits:\n- `2035a69` Summaries and the Reports table\n- `989e6bf` Homepage settings\n- `e9088e3` the homepage and its featured Chart, plus the demo seed\n- `5886258` Site search\n- `29b20f9` glossary\n- `24e2b19` screenshots\n- `05d1f90` review fixes\n- the closing commit\n\nFull suite: **1360 passed** (1289 at the end of T19).\n\n### Code review (`/code-review` since `e540236`, two axes)\n\n#### Standards\n\nNo hard violations. All new links are relative, the new POST has CSRF, `/admin/homepage` is Director-only at the router, the index and the home page read only published items, and `search.js` writes only through `textContent`.\n\n| Finding | Kind | Resolution |\n|---|---|---|\n| `.latest-home p` is a broad selector that reached the Chart's own note and source paragraphs | Documented standard (CSS prefix rule, ADR-007) | **Fixed** in `05d1f90`: `.latest-home-summary` |\n| Context key `description` for the Summary: \"description\" is an _Avoid_ word in CONTEXT.md | Documented standard (vocabulary) | **Fixed**: `meta_description` |\n| `.button-read:hover` hard-codes `#4b2e84` | Judgement | **Fixed**: `--color-kenyon` token, which dark mode leaves alone |\n| Whitespace collapse written three times | Duplicated Code | **Fixed**: `content.one_line`, used by Summaries, Homepage settings, and the Site preview |\n| `.list-search` repeats `.list-data-bites` rule for rule | Duplicated Code | **Fixed**: shared selectors, with one-column overrides |\n| Visually-hidden recipe written twice | Duplicated Code | **Fixed**: one `.text-hidden` utility. The phone table's `thead` keeps its own copy inside the media query, with a comment |\n| `.admin-summary-field` and `.admin-homepage-field` rules identical | Duplicated Code | **Fixed**: one rule |\n| `item_base` hashed items without a Summary the old way | Speculative Generality | **Fixed**: always hashes all four fields. A form opened before the change is refused as stale once, on a local-only console |\n| `homepage` schema in `app/homepage.py`, with `db.py`'s docstring reworded | Divergent Change | **Fixed**: the schema is back in `db.SCHEMA`; `homepage.seed` only inserts the sample row |\n| `SettingsError` has the same shape as `ContentError`; the homepage route builds `error`/`error_field` inline | Duplicated Code | **Kept.** Homepage settings aren't content (CONTEXT.md), so they don't raise `ContentError`. The duplication is two lines |\n| `title, slug, body, summary` travel together through ~12 call sites | Data Clumps / Shotgun Surgery | **Kept.** A real refactor (an item-fields type) but out of T20's scope. Worth a ticket if another field arrives |\n| A search from inside a Site preview leaves the preview for `/search.html` | Note | **Kept.** It's the same as the preview's nav links (`site_file` sends any other page to the published one) |\n\n#### Spec\n\nNothing missing. Every acceptance criterion has code and a test. The differences from the spec's wording are recorded here:\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| The Confirmation reads \"Homepage saved. The public site updates at the next cms publish.\" The spec says \"Homepage saved.\" | **Kept, deliberately.** It is the same `SITE_NOTE` the publish and unpublish Confirmations carry, and the spec says settings appear \"on the next `cms publish`\". Still fixed text, as CONTEXT.md requires |\n| `og:title` is the item's title and `og:type` is `article`/`website`; the spec lists them as places \"a Summary shows\" | **Kept.** That's the only reading that makes sense for those tags: `og:description` and `meta description` carry the Summary |\n| The live count and the server can disagree on rare Unicode whitespace (JS `\\s` vs Python `str.split()`) | **Kept.** It differs by a character on unusual input, and the server's refusal is the rule |\n| Not asked for: the home page's description is its intro | **Kept.** The home page needs some description; the intro is the obvious one |\n| Not asked for: the demo seed now has Summaries, two Charts, and more items | **Kept.** The Director asked for sample data to see the whole design |\n| Not asked for: the headline is required, a Key figure needs both value and label, and line breaks in a Summary or setting become spaces | **Kept.** These keep the homepage from showing an empty `<h1>` or a number with no label |\n\n### Browser check\n\nScratch instance (`cms serve` on its own database in the session scratchpad), and its `cms publish` export served statically for the viewport harness (same-origin iframes, as in T19). Screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/`.\n\n| Check | Result | Screenshot |\n|---|---|---|\n| Edit the homepage (accent \"checked and final.\", figure 1,805 → 1,812), save, see it in a published copy | **Pass.** \"Homepage saved.\" shows. After `cms publish`, the exported `index.html` has both changes | `t20-homepage-settings-saved-1372.jpg`, `site-home-1440-768-390-light.jpg` |\n| Write a Summary and see its count and limit | **Pass.** It counts as typed, turns red at \"218 of 200: 18 too many.\", and the Site preview follows. Saving is refused beside the field (\"Keep the summary to 200 characters or fewer; it has 218.\") and the text is kept | `t20-summary-count-over-limit.jpg`, `t20-summary-refused-by-field.jpg` |\n| Search for a term in a title: \"enrollment\" | **Pass.** 2 results, the title match (Fall enrollment snapshot) above the Summary match (Factbook) | `t20-search-title-term-enrollment.jpg` |\n| Search for a term only in a Summary: \"census\" | **Pass.** 1 result | `t20-search-summary-only-census.jpg` |\n| Search for a term with no match: \"tuition\" | **Pass.** \"Nothing published matches “tuition”.\" | `t20-search-no-match-tuition.jpg` |\n| Home at 1440, 768, and 390 px, light | **Pass.** Atkinson Next and Mono `loaded` at every width (Next italic unused, so unloaded); no sideways scroll; figures four across, then two | `site-home-1440-768-390-light.jpg` |\n| Home at 1440, 768, and 390 px, dark | **Pass.** As above | `site-home-1440-768-390-dark.jpg` |\n| Without JavaScript | **Pass**, by test: `search.html` lists every published item, and no draft | — |\n\n`site-home-*` replaces T19's version, which left out the intro until this ticket.\n\n**Contrast of the new text** (WCAG ratio, light / dark):\n\n| Pair | Light | Dark |\n|---|---|---|\n| Accent and Key-figure notes (bright purple on the field) | 5.35 | 4.62 |\n| Summary under a title, intro (`--color-field-text` on the field) | 11.60 | 12.52 |\n| Muted text (Summaries in lists, the status line) on paper | 6.52 | 7.31 |\n| Search button (field on citron) | 13.60 | 13.60 |\n| Read the Data Bite button (white on the field) | 16.77 | — |\n| Its hover (white on Kenyon purple) | 10.38 | 10.38 |\n\n**Not checked:** Safari, and a share preview in a real Slack or email client. `og:url` and `og:image` are left out by design, so a preview shows the title and Summary only.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":875,"cache_read_input_tokens":318302,"output_tokens":2818,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":0},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":875,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":2818,"cache_read_input_tokens":318302,"cache_creation_input_tokens":875,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":875},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_01JQbJxqM4saDJH3D3qdGdbs":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9020c1e3-a9a3-4f69-ac84-7c257e705f41/scratchpad/t20/closing-comment.md","content":"## A form opened before the change is refused as stale once, on a local-only console |\n| `homepage` schema in `app/homepage.py`, with `db.py`'s docstring reworded | Divergent Change | **Fixed**: the schema is back in `db.SCHEMA`; `homepage.seed` only inserts the sample row |\n| `SettingsError` has the same shape as `ContentError`; the homepage route builds `error`/`error_field` inline | Duplicated Code | **Kept.** Homepage settings aren't content (CONTEXT.md), so they don't raise `ContentError`. The duplication is two lines |\n| `title, slug, body, summary` travel together through ~12 call sites | Data Clumps / Shotgun Surgery | **Kept.** A real refactor (an item-fields type) but out of T20's scope. Worth a ticket if another field arrives |\n| A search from inside a Site preview leaves the preview for `/search.html` | Note | **Kept.** It's the same as the preview's nav links (`site_file` sends any other page to the published one) |\n\n#### Spec\n\nNothing missing. Every acceptance criterion has code and a test. The differences from the spec's wording are recorded here:\n\n| Finding | Resolution |\n|---|---|\n| The Confirmation reads \"Homepage saved. The public site updates at the next cms publish.\" The spec says \"Homepage saved.\" | **Kept, deliberately.** It is the same `SITE_NOTE` the publish and unpublish Confirmations carry, and the spec says settings appear \"on the next `cms publish`\". Still fixed text, as CONTEXT.md requires |\n| `og:title` is the item's title and `og:type` is `article`/`website`; the spec lists them as places \"a Summary shows\" | **Kept.** That's the only reading that makes sense for those tags: `og:description` and `meta description` carry the Summary |\n| The live count and the server can disagree on rare Unicode whitespace (JS `\\s` vs Python `str.split()`) | **Kept.** It differs by a character on unusual input, and the server's refusal is the rule |\n| Not asked for: the home page's description is its intro | **Kept.** The home page needs some description; the intro is the obvious one |\n| Not asked for: the demo seed now has Summaries, two Charts, and more items | **Kept.** The Director asked for sample data to see the whole design |\n| Not asked for: the headline is required, a Key figure needs both value and label, and line breaks in a Summary or setting become spaces | **Kept.** These keep the homepage from showing an empty `<h1>` or a number with no label |\n\n### Browser check\n\nScratch instance (`cms serve` on its own database in the session scratchpad), and its `cms publish` export served statically for the viewport harness (same-origin iframes, as in T19). Screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/`.\n\n| Check | Result | Screenshot |\n|---|---|---|\n| Edit the homepage (accent \"checked and final.\", figure 1,805 → 1,812), save, see it in a published copy | **Pass.** \"Homepage saved.\" shows. After `cms publish`, the exported `index.html` has both changes | `t20-homepage-settings-saved-1372.jpg`, `site-home-1440-768-390-light.jpg` |\n| Write a Summary and see its count and limit | **Pass.** It counts as typed, turns red at \"218 of 200: 18 too many.\", and the Site preview follows. Saving is refused beside the field (\"Keep the summary to 200 characters or fewer; it has 218.\") and the text is kept | `t20-summary-count-over-limit.jpg`, `t20-summary-refused-by-field.jpg` |\n| Search for a term in a title: \"enrollment\" | **Pass.** 2 results, the title match (Fall enrollment snapshot) above the Summary match (Factbook) | `t20-search-title-term-enrollment.jpg` |\n| Search for a term only in a Summary: \"census\" | **Pass.** 1 result | `t20-search-summary-only-census.jpg` |\n| Search for a term with no match: \"tuition\" | **Pass.** \"Nothing published matches “tuition”.\" | `t20-search-no-match-tuition.jpg` |\n| Home at 1440, 768, and 390 px, light | **Pass.** Atkinson Next and Mono `loaded` at every width (Next italic unused, so unloaded); no sideways scroll; figures four across, then two | `site-home-1440-768-390-light.jpg` |\n| Home at 1440, 768, and 390 px, dark | **Pass.** As above | `site-home-1440-768-390-dark.jpg` |\n| Without JavaScript | **Pass**, by test: `search.html` lists every published item, and no draft | — |\n\n`site-home-*` replaces T19's version, which left out the intro until this ticket.\n\n**Contrast of the new text** (WCAG ratio, light / dark):\n\n| Pair | Light | Dark |\n|---|---|---|\n| Accent and Key-figure notes (bright purple on the field) | 5.35 | 4.62 |\n| Summary under a title, intro (`--color-field-text` on the field) | 11.60 | 12.52 |\n| Muted text (Summaries in lists, the status line) on paper | 6.52 | 7.31 |\n| Search button (field on citron) | 13.60 | 13.60 |\n| Read the Data Bite button (white on the field) | 16.77 | — |\n| Its hover (white on Kenyon purple) | 10.38 | 10.38 |\n\n**Not checked:** Safari, and a share preview in a real Slack or email client. `og:url` and `og:image` are left out by design, so a preview shows the title and Summary only.\n","structuredPatch":[],"originalFile":null,"userModified":false},"sourceToolAssistantUUID":"28b49e10-dc05-4bb6-a018-36a69acee6fd","session_id":"d5c3385e-b66b-4027-9837-a0bfd3de9dbc","userType":"external","entrypoint":"cli","cwd":"/Users/davelleat/code/iphs400-mp2-cms","sessionId":"9020c1e3-a9a3-4f69-ac84-7c257e705f41","version":"2.1.285","gitBranch":"main"}

Print: same trick on `@media print`. Report `document.fonts` statuses and `scrollWidth > innerWidth` in the harness's status line.\n- **Screenshot `scale` also shrinks the saved file**: use scale 1 with `save_to_disk` for anything going in docs/screenshots.\n- **Programmatic `.focus()` in a frame doesn't match `:focus`** (no window focus); press real Tab keys on the page itself (the first Tab lands in browser chrome).\n- **Claude in Chrome's resize_window doesn't change the viewport** (stayed 516 px, or whatever the window is). 768/1440 px checks can't be done that way.\n- **gstack `browse` (headless) is killed by the command sandbox** (exit 137), and running it with the sandbox disabled was refused by the auto-mode classifier. Don't retry; ask the user.\n- **390 px for anything besides the public page** (e.g. a dialog): put a same-origin `<iframe src=\"/admin/...\">` 390 px wide on an admin page and drive it; its `innerWidth` is 390 and media queries apply. Keep it ≤740 px tall so the screenshot (scaled ~1.14×) shows it whole.\n- **Port 8001 may already be taken** by a leftover T15 scratch `cms serve` (its own scratch DB); check `lsof -ti :8001` and use another port rather than trusting it.\n- **Phone width works through the app itself**: the Site preview's **Phone** toggle frames the page at 390 px (388 inside).\n- **Real Excel/Sheets pastes need the user**: OS keystrokes via osascript stall on a permission prompt. The user pastes by hand; Claude reads the saved draft back.\n- **Scratch instance**: run `cms serve --port 8001` with `CMS_DATABASE`/`CMS_UPLOADS` in the session scratchpad and `scripts/seed_demo.py` passwords set by env, so checks never touch the real `cms.db`.\n- The user has accepted \"not checked\" for Safari and 768/1440 on T15 and T16, recorded on the issue.\n- **Click by element ref, not coordinates**: the screenshot coordinate frame switches between e.g. 1372×872 and 1200×763 within one session, so coordinate clicks miss (T18 typed a description into the body). Use `find` refs.\n- **Leaving a dirty Editor page** without the beforeunload dialog: add a submit listener that calls `preventDefault()`, then dispatch a synthetic `SubmitEvent` on the form. The Editor's own listener sets its \"leaving\" flag, and nothing is posted.\n- **A cached editor.js** can survive a server restart; `fetch(src, {cache: \"reload\"})` then navigate again.\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":5,"oldLines":7,"newStart":5,"newLines":7,"lines":["   node_type: memory","   type: reference","   originSessionId: 6d83085c-4859-4681-9c06-b59afa52f437","-  modified: 2026-10-01T15:44:20.809Z","+  modified: 2026-10-01T19:12:26.566Z"," ---"," "," Browser checks for closing comments (spec #14) in this environment, as of 2026-10-01:"]},{"oldStart":23,"oldLines":4,"newStart":23,"newLines":6,"lines":[" - The user has accepted \"not checked\" for Safari and 768/1440 on T15 and T16, recorded on the issue."," - **Click by element ref, not coordinates**: the screenshot coordinate frame switches between e.g. 1372×872 and 1200×763 within one session, so coordinate clicks miss (T18 typed a description into the body). {"parentUuid":"3d6622c8-95e7-4f29-af55-748b8c34515a","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfc3mG1r7uvi9t9NNViBh","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"T20 is finished and committed locally. #24 is still **open** because `main` is 8 commits ahead of `origin/main` and isn't pushed yet. The closing commit (`5e5814b`) ends with `Closes #24`, so pushing will close it. I haven't pushed; just say so if you want me to.\n\n**Steps 7–8:**\n- **Browser check:** every check passed:\n  - The homepage edit, after saving, showed \"Homepage saved.\" and appeared in the published copy.\n  - A Summary over 200 characters turned the count red (\"218 of 200\") and was refused beside the field.\n  - The three searches gave the expected results: \"enrollment\" from a title, \"census\" from a summary only, and \"tuition\" with no match.\n  - The home page at 1440/768/390 px in light and dark had both fonts loaded and no sideways scroll.\n  - Every new text colour meets the WCAG AA contrast standard; the lowest is 4.62:1.\n  - Screenshots are in `docs/screenshots/`.\n- **Code review:** two passes, one against the repo's standards and one against the spec.\n  - **Standards:** no hard violations or bugs. I fixed 9 of the 12 judgement calls in `05d1f90`, including:\n    - a CSS rule that reached into the chart's own text;\n    - a variable named with a word `CONTEXT.md` says to avoid;\n    - duplicated CSS and code;\n    - the homepage table's schema, which now lives in `db.py` with the other tables.\n  - **Spec:** nothing missing. It noted a few places I went slightly past the spec's wording. I kept them and explained why in the comment.\n- **Closing comment** is posted on #24 with each finding and how it was resolved, the browser-check table, and the contrast ratios: https://github.com/DavelleAT/iphs400-mp2-cms/issues/24#issuecomment-5938672768\n- **Full suite:** 1360 tests pass.\n\nTwo things in the comment you may want to look at:\n- **Confirmation text:** it reads \"Homepage saved. The .content-body and .chart-* rules are here\n   for the Editor's body and the Chart builder's preview. */\n:root { color-scheme: light dark; }\nbody { font: 16px/1.6 system-ui, sans-serif; margin: 0 auto; max-width: 42rem; padding: 1rem; }\n.header-home { font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; }\nmain { margin-block: 2rem; }\n/* Admin only: the message after a successful save (app.flash). */\n.admin-confirmation { background: color-mix(in srgb, #2e7d32 12%, transparent); border-left: 4px solid #2e7d32; margin: 0 0 1.5rem; padding: 0.6rem 0.9rem; }\n/* Markdown tables, in a Data Bite's or Report's body. Each is\n   drawn twice; the narrow drawing replaces the wide one on a phone, and\n   display: none takes the hidden one out of the accessibility tree. */\n.chart-figure { margin: 1.5rem 0; }\n.chart-title { font-weight: 600; } }\n.chart-figure text { font-family: system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 13px; }\n.chart-figure polyline { stroke-linecap: round; stroke-linejoin: round; }\n.chart-figure circle { stroke: Canvas; }\n.chart-note, .chart-source { margin: 0.25rem 0; src: url(\"../../../static/fonts/atkinson-hyperlegible-mono-latin-wght-normal.woff2\") format(\"woff2\"); font-weight: 200 800; font-style: normal; font-display: swap; }\n\n:root {\n  color-scheme: light dark;\n  --font-text: \"Atkinson Next\", system-ui, sans-serif;\n  --font-mono: \"Atkinson Mono\", ui-monospace, monospace;\n  --color-paper: #fbfafd;\n  --color-surface: #ffffff; }\nbody { background: var(--color-paper); color: var(--color-ink); font: 400 1rem/1.6 var(--font-text); margin: 0; }\na { color: var(--color-purple); text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.2em; }\n:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid var(--color-bright); outline-offset: 2px; }\nh1, h2, h3 { font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: -0.02em; line-height: 1.15; margin: 0; }\n.text-mono { font-family: var(--font-mono); }\n.text-hidden { clip-path: inset(50%); height: 1px; overflow: hidden; position: absolute; white-space: nowrap; width: 1px; }\n\n/* The slim bar: the field, its grid, the mark, numbered nav, who's signed in. */\n.bar-console { background-color: var(--color-field); }\n}\n\n/* A page: its head (breadcrumb, title, facts, its main action), then sections. */\n.page-console { margin-inline: auto; max-width: var(--width-page); padding: clamp(1.25rem, 3vw, 2.25rem) clamp(1rem, 3vw, 2rem) 6rem; {"parentUuid":"3acacd19-5c45-4d37-85f6-44f251fa0fea","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfc4NPz4QvTiGun91utTX","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The console mockup is ready for your review. It's a static mockup: nothing in the app has changed, and I haven't committed it. Session 22's mockup was only committed once approved, so this one waits for your yes too.\n\n**Open it:** http://localhost:8002/docs/design/admin-console-mockup/index.html. The nav links between the dashboard, the Data Bites list, and the edit page. Screenshots at 1440/768/390 px, in light and dark, are in `docs/design/admin-console-mockup/screenshots/`:\n- `dashboard-1440-768-390-light.jpg` and `-dark.jpg`\n- `data-bites-1440-768-390-light.jpg`\n- `edit-1440-768-390-light.jpg` and `-dark.jpg`\n\n**What it does:**\n- **Look:** the public site's fonts, colours, numbered labels and ISO dates, on light paper. The deep purple appears only as a slim top bar, and citron (the yellow-green) only in that bar.\n- **Navigation on every page:** 01 Dashboard, 02 Data Bites, 03 Reports, 04 Homepage, 05 Users, plus who's signed in, \"View site ↗\", and Log out. On a phone the menu scrolls sideways under the bar, like the public nav.\n- **Dashboard:** four counts, then \"01 Waiting for you\". For the Director, that's draft Reports only they can publish. Then \"02 Recently changed\", with side panels for publishing the site and editing the homepage.\n- **Lists:** a table with each Summary under its title, status badges (● Published, a dashed Draft, \"Ready to publish\"), filter tabs with counts, and Edit / Publish on each row. \"New Data Bite\" is a button, so the create form no longer sits under the list.\n- **Edit page:**\n  - The fields and Editor sit on the left; the slug is shown as an address (`data-bites/` + slug + `.html`), and the Editor gets a grouped toolbar.\n  - The Site preview stays in view on the right.\n  - A save bar is pinned to the bottom: status, an \"Unsaved changes\" marker, Delete, Unpublish, and Save.\n\n**Checked:** both fonts load, and nothing scrolls sideways at any width in either theme. On a phone, \"Log out\" wrapped onto its own line at first; I fixed that by hiding the bar's long label below 40rem.\n\n**Next step:** tell me what to change, or approve it as it is. Once you approve, I'll commit it and write the spec and tickets on GitHub. {"parentUuid":"94247806-5866-4e01-8e6f-9302b409881c","isSidechain":false,"promptId":"6737b2f6-1235-4113-8a56-6532699aaf2f","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_013RKVZEtMzUgJET9KTrCZvo","type":"tool_result","content":"260fe8b docs: the approved admin console mockup, same family as the public site, calmer\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. Use the `gh` CLI for all operations.\n\n## Conventions\n\n- **Create an issue**: `gh issue create --title \"...\" --body \"...\"`. Use a heredoc for multi-line bodies.\n- **Read an issue**: `gh issue view <number> --comments`, filtering comments by `jq` and also fetching labels.\n- **List issues**: `gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,comments --jq '[.[] | {number, title, body, labels: [.labels[].name], comments: [.comments[].body]}]'` with appropriate `--label` and `--state` filters.\n- **Comment on an issue**: `gh issue comment <number> --body \"...\"`\n- **Apply / remove labels**: `gh issue edit <number> --add-label \"...\"` / `--remove-label \"...\"`\n- **Close**: `gh issue close <number> --comment \"...\"`\n\nInfer the repo from `git remote -v`; `gh` does this automatically when run inside a clone.\n\n## Pull requests as a triage surface\n\n**PRs as a request surface: no.** _(Set to `yes` if this repo treats external PRs as feature requests; `/triage` reads this flag.)_\n\nWhen set to `yes`, PRs run through the same labels and states as issues, using the `gh pr` equivalents:\n\n- **Read a PR**: `gh pr view <number> --comments` and `gh pr diff <number>` for the diff.\n- **List external PRs for triage**: `gh pr list --state open --json number,title,body,labels,author,authorAssociation,comments` then keep only `authorAssociation` of `CONTRIBUTOR`, `FIRST_TIME_CONTRIBUTOR`, or `NONE` (drop `OWNER`/`MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR`).\n- **Comment / label / close**: `gh pr comment`, `gh pr edit --add-label`/`--remove-label`, `gh pr close`.\n\nGitHub shares one number space across issues and PRs, so a bare `#42` may be either: resolve with `gh pr view 42` and fall back to `gh issue view 42`.\n\n## When a skill says \"publish to the issue tracker\"\n\nCreate a GitHub issue.\n\n## When a skill says \"fetch the relevant ticket\"\n\nRun `gh issue view <number> --comments`.\n\n## Wayfinding operations\n\nUsed by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a single issue with **child** issues as tickets.\n\n- **Map**: a single issue labelled `wayfinder:map`, holding the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body. `gh issue create --label wayfinder:map`.\napp/routes/auth.py:47:def admin_stylesheet():","is_error":false}]},"uuid":"91579d15-d221-4f50-bd5c-42ecbbdacbeb","timestamp":"2026-10-01T19:22:21.575Z","toolUseResult":{"stdout":"260fe8b docs: the approved admin console mockup, same family as the public site, calmer\n# Issue tracker: GitHub\n\nIssues and specs for this repo live as GitHub issues. {"parentUuid":"7f390cca-def0-4c8f-bd8f-0b818a1d3e9b","isSidechain":false,"message":{"model":"claude-opus-5-5","id":"msg_011Cfc4XNEPKHsibQ4jE2UYf","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"toolu_014Vi76Xy86rQhwXtEUvxw5Q","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9020c1e3-a9a3-4f69-ac84-7c257e705f41/scratchpad/spec-console.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe public site was redesigned in T19 and T20, but the admin console the Director and Analysts use every day still has no design: the system font, browser-grey buttons, monospace text boxes, and one 42rem column. It is also hard to use:\n\n- **No navigation.** The only way between pages is an \"All Data Bites\" or \"Admin console\" back-link, and Log out is a button that only exists on the admin home.\n- **Crowded list pages.** The Data Bites and Reports list pages also hold the whole create form, the Editor, and a Site preview, so the list sits on top of a long form.\n- **A dashboard that doesn't help.** It is a table of counts, and nothing says what needs attention, such as a draft Report only the Director can publish.\n- **A cramped edit page.** The fields, Editor, and Site preview stack in one column, and Save sits under a long body.\n\nGoal: a console that is as considered as the public site and pleasant to use for hours, which shows each person what needs their attention first.\n\n## Solution\n\nA visual design, **\"same family, calmer\"**, approved from a mockup in session 25. The mockup and its screenshots are in `docs/design/admin-console-mockup/`.\n\n- **Type and colour:** the public site's Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono, and its tokens, on light paper throughout. The deep purple field appears only as a slim top bar with its faint grid. Citron appears only in that bar, as the IR mark and the current-page underline. A full dark mode.\n- **Structure:** numbered nav, numbered sections, ISO dates in mono, square status badges, hairline tables, and square buttons with one solid action per view.\n\nAnd four usability changes:\n\n- **Navigation on every page:** 01 Dashboard, 02 Data Bites, 03 Reports, and, for the Director, 04 Homepage and 05 Users. Plus who is signed in, \"View site ↗\", and Log out.\n- **Lists apart from forms:** each list is a table with Summaries, status badges, filters, and row actions. Creating an item opens its own page.\n- **A dashboard of what needs attention:** counts, \"Waiting for you\", and \"Recently changed\".\n- **An edit page laid out for work:** the fields and Editor beside a sticky Site preview, and a save bar pinned to the bottom.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As the Director, I want to see, on signing in, which draft Reports are waiting for me to publish, so that nothing sits unreviewed.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to see my own drafts first on the dashboard, so that I pick up where I left off, or where the last shift left off.\n3. As any user, I want the same navigation on every console page, so that I never hunt for a back-link.\n4. As any user, I want to log out from any page.\n5. As any user, I want each list to show every item's Summary, state, author, and last update, and to filter by state, so that I find an item without opening it.\n6. As any user, I want \"New Data Bite\" to open its own page, so that the list stays a list.\n7. As any user, I want the Site preview beside the fields while I edit, and Save always in reach, so that I don't scroll past a long body to save.\n8. As any user, I want to know when I have unsaved changes before I leave.\n9. As any user, I want an item's address shown as `data-bites/<slug>.html`, so that the slug is understandable.\n10. As any user on a laptop at night, I want the console to follow dark mode.\n11. As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want a skip link, a visible focus ring, labelled fields, and AA contrast in the console too.\n12. As the Director, I want the Users and Homepage pages to look and work like the rest of the console.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Shared (ADR-007 stays: two stylesheets, no rule crosses)\n\n- **`static/admin.css` is rewritten** as the console's own stylesheet. It copies the public tokens and the `@font-face` rules, and never links or imports `site.css`. No public rule may reach an admin page, and no admin rule may reach the public site (the T19 tests stay).\n- **Fonts:** `admin.css` is served at `/admin.css`, so its `url(\"fonts/…\")` resolves to `/fonts/…`, which the public route already serves. No new route and no new dependency.\n- **Class names** keep the repo's prefix rule: `.bar-console`, `.nav-console`, `.badge-state-draft`, `.table-items`, `.bar-save`. No bare `.title` or `.status`.\n- **The Editor and the Chart builder are restyled by class only.** `static/editor.js` keeps its markup, classes, and behaviour. In the console, Chart cards use the public site's purples and greys instead of today's blue and orange.\n- **No new database columns.** \"Waiting for you\" is derived from what is stored: a draft Report is waiting for the Director, and an Analyst's own drafts are theirs.\n- **Accessibility:** skip link, `:focus-visible` ring, labelled fields, and text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in both themes, recorded in each closing comment.\n\n### T21: Console shell\n\n- `base.html` becomes the console layout:\n  - The slim bar with the IR mark and \"Console\".\n  - Numbered nav. Homepage and Users show only for a Director. `aria-current` marks the current section.\n  - The signed-in user's name and role, \"View site ↗\" to the public home, and Log out (a POST with CSRF) on every signed-in page.\n  - A skip link and the Confirmation, restyled.\n- On a phone, the nav scrolls sideways under the bar and never wraps, as on the public site.\n- The login, \"Not allowed\" (403), confirm-delete, Users, and Homepage settings pages move to the new look and type. They keep their behaviour.\n- Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`.\n\n### T22: Lists and create pages\n\n- `/admin/data-bites` and `/admin/reports` become `table-items` tables:\n  - Columns: title with its Summary under it, a state badge, author, Updated (ISO), and row actions (Edit, Publish/Unpublish, and Delete for a Director). Each action is a POST with CSRF, as now.\n  - Filters: All / Published / Drafts, each with its count, via `?status=`. An unknown value is a 400, as on the All content page.\n  - A \"New Data Bite\" or \"New Report\" button in the page head.\n- The create forms move to `/admin/data-bites/new` and `/admin/reports/new`, laid out like the edit page. The POST target stays `/admin/data-bites` and `/admin/reports`.\n- **After a create, the redirect goes to the new item's edit page**, not the list. Tests that assert the old location are updated in the same commit, with the reason.\n- The All content page uses the same table.\n- Rows stack on a phone. The table keeps its semantics, as in T20's Reports table.\n\n### T23: Edit pages\n\n- Two columns at desktop width, one below 64rem:\n  - Left: Title (large), Summary with its count, the slug as an address field (`data-bites/` [slug] `.html`), and the Editor.\n  - Right: the Site preview with Desktop / Phone and \"Open ↗\", sticky.\n- **A save bar pinned to the bottom** shows the state badge, an \"Unsaved changes\" marker, Save, and Publish/Unpublish and Delete where the user may do them. Buttons outside the item's form use the `form=` attribute or their own small forms. No action may lose CSRF or the stale-form check (`item_base`).\n- The \"Unsaved changes\" marker follows the Editor's existing dirty state (`body_dirty`) and any field's `input` event.\n- A Report's PDF field and its chart images sit under the Editor.\n- A Report that is locked for an Analyst keeps today's read-only view, in the new layout.\n\n### T24: Dashboard\n\n- Head: \"Dashboard\", today's date, the user's role, and \"New Data Bite\" (plus \"New Report\").\n- Four counts (Data Bites published and drafts, Reports published and drafts), each linking to its filtered list.\n- **01 Waiting for you:**\n  - For a Director: draft Reports, oldest update first, each with \"Review\".\n  - For an Analyst: their own drafts, Data Bites and Reports.\n  - Empty, it says so.\n- **02 Recently changed:** the 8 most recently updated items of both kinds, with a state badge and an ISO date, and a link to All content.\n- **Side panels:** \"The public site\" (publishing reaches it at the next `cms publish`, plus \"View the site ↗\"), and, for a Director, \"Homepage\" (when it was last saved, plus \"Edit homepage\").\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Existing tests keep passing. A test that asserts on today's console markup or a redirect location is updated in the same commit, with the reason.\n- New tests:\n  - Every signed-in console page has the nav and a Log out form with a CSRF token.\n  - An Analyst's nav has no Homepage or Users link.\n  - No admin page links `style.css`; no public page links `admin.css` (kept from T19).\n  - Each list's filter shows only that state, and a bad `?status=` is a 400.\n  - `/admin/data-bites/new` and `/admin/reports/new` render the form, and a create redirects to the new item's edit page.\n  - The edit page's save-bar buttons each post with a CSRF token. A stale form is still refused (409).\n  - \"Waiting for you\": a Director sees draft Reports and not published ones. An Analyst sees their own drafts and not another Analyst's. Nothing from it leaks to a public page.\n- **Browser check** in each closing comment, at 390, 768, and 1440 px in light and dark, with screenshots and `document.fonts`. That covers the nav, a list, a create, an edit with the save bar and the unsaved marker, the dashboard as the Director and as an Analyst, and the Users and Homepage pages.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Any change to the public site.\n- New roles, a review or approval workflow, or a \"submit for review\" state. \"Waiting for you\" is derived from existing states.\n- Recording when `cms publish` last ran.\n- Search in the console.\n- Changes to the Editor's behaviour or the Chart builder's features. They are restyled only.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Mockup: `docs/design/admin-console-mockup/` (`index.html`, `data-bites.html`, `edit.html`, `console.css`, and `screenshots/`). Its CSS is the starting point for `static/admin.css`.\n- Stage 2 is due Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern. The tickets are ordered so that each one leaves the console working and committed: T21, then T22, then T23, then T24.\n"},"caller":{"type":"direct"}}],"container":null,"stop_reason":"tool_use","stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1027,"cache_read_input_tokens":390387,"output_tokens":4128,"output_tokens_details":{"thinking_tokens":134},"server_tool_use":{"web_search_requests":0,"web_fetch_requests":0},"service_tier":"standard","cache_creation":{"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1027,"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0},"inference_geo":"not_available","iterations":[{"input_tokens":2,"output_tokens":4128,"cache_read_input_tokens":390387,"cache_creation_input_tokens":1027,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":1027},"type":"message"}],"speed":"standard","fallback_credit":null},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"wireToolInputs":{"toolu_014Vi76Xy86rQhwXtEUvxw5Q":{"file_path":"/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-davelleat-code-iphs400-mp2-cms/9020c1e3-a9a3-4f69-ac84-7c257e705f41/scratchpad/spec-console.md","content":"## Problem Statement\n\nThe public site was redesigned in T19 and T20, but the admin console the Director and Analysts use every day still has no design: the system font, browser-grey buttons, monospace text boxes, and one 42rem column. As any user, I want to know when I have unsaved changes before I leave.\n9. As any user, I want an item's address shown as `data-bites/<slug>.html`, so that the slug is understandable.\n10. As any user on a laptop at night, I want the console to follow dark mode.\n11. As a keyboard or screen-reader user, I want a skip link, a visible focus ring, labelled fields, and AA contrast in the console too.\n12. As the Director, I want the Users and Homepage pages to look and work like the rest of the console.\n\n## Implementation Decisions\n\n### Shared (ADR-007 stays: two stylesheets, no rule crosses)\n\n- **`static/admin.css` is rewritten** as the console's own stylesheet. It copies the public tokens and the `@font-face` rules, and never links or imports `site.css`. No public rule may reach an admin page, and no admin rule may reach the public site (the T19 tests stay).\n- **Fonts:** `admin.css` is served at `/admin.css`, so its `url(\"fonts/…\")` resolves to `/fonts/…`, which the public route already serves. No new route and no new dependency.\n- **Class names** keep the repo's prefix rule: `.bar-console`, `.nav-console`, `.badge-state-draft`, `.table-items`, `.bar-save`. No bare `.title` or `.status`.\n- **The Editor and the Chart builder are restyled by class only.** `static/editor.js` keeps its markup, classes, and behaviour. In the console, Chart cards use the public site's purples and greys instead of today's blue and orange.\n- **No new database columns.** \"Waiting for you\" is derived from what is stored: a draft Report is waiting for the Director, and an Analyst's own drafts are theirs.\n- **Accessibility:** skip link, `:focus-visible` ring, labelled fields, and text contrast ≥ 4.5:1 in both themes, recorded in each closing comment.\n\n### T21: Console shell\n\n- `base.html` becomes the console layout:\n  - The slim bar with the IR mark and \"Console\".\n  - Numbered nav. Homepage and Users show only for a Director. `aria-current` marks the current section.\n  - The signed-in user's name and role, \"View site ↗\" to the public home, and Log out (a POST with CSRF) on every signed-in page.\n  - A skip link and the Confirmation, restyled.\n- On a phone, the nav scrolls sideways under the bar and never wraps, as on the public site.\n- The login, \"Not allowed\" (403), confirm-delete, Users, and Homepage settings pages move to the new look and type. They keep their behaviour.\n- Dark mode via `prefers-color-scheme`.\n\n### T22: Lists and create pages\n\n- `/admin/data-bites` and `/admin/reports` become `table-items` tables:\n  - Columns: title with its Summary under it, a state badge, author, Updated (ISO), and row actions (Edit, Publish/Unpublish, and Delete for a Director). Each action is a POST with CSRF, as now.\n  - Filters: All / Published / Drafts, each with its count, via `?status=`. An unknown value is a 400, as on the All content page.\n  - A \"New Data Bite\" or \"New Report\" button in the page head.\n- The create forms move to `/admin/data-bites/new` and `/admin/reports/new`, laid out like the edit page. The POST target stays `/admin/data-bites` and `/admin/reports`.\n- **After a create, the redirect goes to the new item's edit page**, not the list. Tests that assert the old location are updated in the same commit, with the reason.\n- The All content page uses the same table.\n- Rows stack on a phone. The table keeps its semantics, as in T20's Reports table.\n\n### T23: Edit pages\n\n- Two columns at desktop width, one below 64rem:\n  - Left: Title (large), Summary with its count, the slug as an address field (`data-bites/` [slug] `.html`), and the Editor.\n  - Right: the Site preview with Desktop / Phone and \"Open ↗\", sticky.\n- **A save bar pinned to the bottom** shows the state badge, an \"Unsaved changes\" marker, Save, and Publish/Unpublish and Delete where the user may do them. Buttons outside the item's form use the `form=` attribute or their own small forms. No action may lose CSRF or the stale-form check (`item_base`).\n- The \"Unsaved changes\" marker follows the Editor's existing dirty state (`body_dirty`) and any field's `input` event.\n- A Report's PDF field and its chart images sit under the Editor.\n- A Report that is locked for an Analyst keeps today's read-only view, in the new layout.\n\n### T24: Dashboard\n\n- Head: \"Dashboard\", today's date, the user's role, and \"New Data Bite\" (plus \"New Report\").\n- Four counts (Data Bites published and drafts, Reports published and drafts), each linking to its filtered list.\n- **01 Waiting for you:**\n  - For a Director: draft Reports, oldest update first, each with \"Review\".\n  - For an Analyst: their own drafts, Data Bites and Reports.\n  - Empty, it says so.\n- **02 Recently changed:** the 8 most recently updated items of both kinds, with a state badge and an ISO date, and a link to All content.\n- **Side panels:** \"The public site\" (publishing reaches it at the next `cms publish`, plus \"View the site ↗\"), and, for a Director, \"Homepage\" (when it was last saved, plus \"Edit homepage\").\n\n## Testing Decisions\n\n- Existing tests keep passing. A test that asserts on today's console markup or a redirect location is updated in the same commit, with the reason.\n- New tests:\n  - Every signed-in console page has the nav and a Log out form with a CSRF token.\n  - An Analyst's nav has no Homepage or Users link.\n  - No admin page links `style.css`; no public page links `admin.css` (kept from T19).\n  - Each list's filter shows only that state, and a bad `?status=` is a 400.\n  - `/admin/data-bites/new` and `/admin/reports/new` render the form, and a create redirects to the new item's edit page.\n  - The edit page's save-bar buttons each post with a CSRF token. A stale form is still refused (409).\n  - \"Waiting for you\": a Director sees draft Reports and not published ones. An Analyst sees their own drafts and not another Analyst's. Nothing from it leaks to a public page.\n- **Browser check** in each closing comment, at 390, 768, and 1440 px in light and dark, with screenshots and `document.fonts`. That covers the nav, a list, a create, an edit with the save bar and the unsaved marker, the dashboard as the Director and as an Analyst, and the Users and Homepage pages.\n\n## Out of Scope\n\n- Any change to the public site.\n- New roles, a review or approval workflow, or a \"submit for review\" state. \"Waiting for you\" is derived from existing states.\n- Recording when `cms publish` last ran.\n- Search in the console.\n- Changes to the Editor's behaviour or the Chart builder's features. They are restyled only.\n\n## Further Notes\n\n- Mockup: `docs/design/admin-console-mockup/` (`index.html`, `data-bites.html`, `edit.html`, `console.css`, and `screenshots/`). Its CSS is the starting point for `static/admin.css`.\n- Stage 2 is due Tue Oct 6, 2:40 pm Eastern. It is also hard to use:\n\n- **No navigation.** The only way between pages is an \"All Data Bites\" or \"Admin console\" back-link, and Log out is a button that only exists on the admin home.\n- **Crowded list pages.** The Data Bites and Reports list pages also hold the whole create form, the Editor, and a Site preview, so the list sits on top of a long form.\n- **A dashboard that doesn't help.** It is a table of counts, and nothing says what needs attention, such as a draft Report only the Director can publish.\n- **A cramped edit page.** The fields, Editor, and Site preview stack in one column, and Save sits under a long body.\n\nGoal: a console that is as considered as the public site and pleasant to use for hours, which shows each person what needs their attention first.\n\n## Solution\n\nA visual design, **\"same family, calmer\"**, approved from a mockup in session 25. The mockup and its screenshots are in `docs/design/admin-console-mockup/`.\n\n- **Type and colour:** the public site's Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono, and its tokens, on light paper throughout. The deep purple field appears only as a slim top bar with its faint grid. Citron appears only in that bar, as the IR mark and the current-page underline. A full dark mode.\n- **Structure:** numbered nav, numbered sections, ISO dates in mono, square status badges, hairline tables, and square buttons with one solid action per view.\n\nAnd four usability changes:\n\n- **Navigation on every page:** 01 Dashboard, 02 Data Bites, 03 Reports, and, for the Director, 04 Homepage and 05 Users. Plus who is signed in, \"View site ↗\", and Log out.\n- **Lists apart from forms:** each list is a table with Summaries, status badges, filters, and row actions. Creating an item opens its own page.\n- **A dashboard of what needs attention:** counts, \"Waiting for you\", and \"Recently changed\".\n- **An edit page laid out for work:** the fields and Editor beside a sticky Site preview, and a save bar pinned to the bottom.\n\n## User Stories\n\n1. As the Director, I want to see, on signing in, which draft Reports are waiting for me to publish, so that nothing sits unreviewed.\n2. As an Analyst, I want to see my own drafts first on the dashboard, so that I pick up where I left off, or where the last shift left off.\n3. As any user, I want the same navigation on every console page, so that I never hunt for a back-link.\n4. As any user, I want to log out from any page.\n5. As any user, I want each list to show every item's Summary, state, author, and last update, and to filter by state, so that I find an item without opening it.\n6. As any user, I want \"New Data Bite\" to open its own page, so that the list stays a list.\n7.
